text: Last week, Maria went to a government office to get a new identity card. She had to fill in a long form with her personal information. First, she wrote her name and surname, and then her birthplace. Maria was born in a small town, but now she lives in the city, so she also wrote her new address. The form asked about her nationality and her occupation — she works as a nurse. Maria is married, not single, so she wrote her husband's name too. After that, she needed to sign the document. Her signature had to look exactly like the one on her passport. The clerk checked her identity card and passport together. He also asked for her phone number and email address, in case the office needed to write to her later. Finally, he said that a new card for a male or female applicant usually takes two weeks. Maria left the office and hoped her new card would arrive soon.
